main_text.p: Haud aliter si quando pios (quum sedibus errant, Securi rerum, varijs) Deus hostibus vrget, Hostibus infandis furias nil praeter, & ignem Qui spirent, Christi populum temerare cruentis Ausi omnes diri manibus, quíque omnia turbent: Huc videas plebem inualidam, puerósque senésque, Tot cunas etiam infantum, matrésque viróque Conflucre, & longè crudeles linquere terras.

Ecce pijs ferunt profugis deserta locorum, Et nemora & montes praerupta & confraga rupium. Heu adeò ingentem terris ex omnibus vndam Huc gentis profugae vomit infelix Europa! En sese huc trepidi per tot discrimina vitae, Mortali, vnanimes, haud sub pastore receptant: Crescit & his demùm praeclara Geneua colonis, Surgit vt exiguo de fonte ingentibus Isler Auctus aquis, aut fluminibus centum Albula dives.

Haec quanquam munita armis, & ponte quaterno Et muro duplici, fossáque & turribus altis: Hanc Cerui Pluteíque licet multo aggere vallent: Se tamen vna Deo propugnatore tuetur Contra tot gladios, hostésque inter rita perstans.

Sic gracilis, geminú sed què mare verberat, Isthmos Nunc salis Ionij furias eludit inanes, Nunc rabiem superi frangit maris; impete magno Irrumpat licet, & magno se turbine voluat. Quin, & vtrumq; simul quum perfurit, altáq; feruet Tempestas vtriusque maris, mugitáque planctu Littora raucisono quatit, horrendúmque sonoris Fluctibus: ille suo contrà se robore firmans Immotus, mundi instar habet, pelagíque furorem Despicit; & terram mordet securus vtramque.
Ergo Deus nimium indigno Regúmq; Ducúmq; Seruitio exemptam, diraéque tyrannide noxis,

page.notes: Two reading uncertainties: "Ergo Deus nimium indigno" line 1 reads "Eᵣgo", possibly "Ergo"; the final word "noxis" was read as "noßis"/"noxis" and is doubtful. Also "Isler" (Isara/Isère) and "Pluteíque" may be mis-printings or unusual forms, and the line "Surgit vt exiguo" is copied as printed. The line "Sic gracilis, geminú sed què mare" has an abbreviation mark on "què" as printed. The leaf is cut at the bottom, so the last line may continue beyond the scan. Strictly, the "Haud" opening is a full paragraph start and I have transcribed it as one; the poem is in verse, but the printer set it as continuous lines, so these are written as paragraphs of verse lines with the line breaks marked by spaces.
